title: Bhai Maharaj Singh
hook: a Sikh saint who resisted the British was exiled and died in Singapore, where Sikhs remember him

segments.voice: Yesterday, a family table and a big question, and your line was who are we. What answer stayed with you? Today, one man who seemed very sure of his. Day nine hundred fifty-four.

Singapore, a busy port city far across the sea from Punjab. In a gurdwara there, the sangat keeps a memorial to a Sikh holy man from Punjab. He didn't come to Singapore to trade, or to serve in a regiment. He came as a prisoner, sent far away from Punjab on purpose. He never went home. But the people who remember him there have made sure he isn't forgotten. Today: Bhai Maharaj Singh.
screen: `A MEMORIAL IN SINGAPORE.` → `HE CAME AS A PRISONER.` → `HE NEVER WENT HOME.`

segments.voice: First, the saint. Bhai Maharaj Singh was a holy man in Punjab, the head of a dera, a religious center, where people came for his blessing and for langar. Bhai is a title of respect, meaning brother. People came to him for his devotion first; the resistance came later. Second, the resister. As the British took control of Punjab, he would not accept it. Sikh histories remember him moving through the countryside after the wars, encouraging resistance and refusing to surrender. The British saw him as dangerous: a respected holy man who could gather people around him. Third, the exile. When he was finally captured, the British didn't keep him in Punjab, where people might gather around him again. They sent him across the sea to Singapore and held him in prison there. Cut off from his people, his health failed, and he died in exile. Fourth, the line that fits him. In the saloks of Guru Tegh Bahadur, near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Guru says the wise one frightens no one and is afraid of no one. That is how Sikh tellings remember Bhai Maharaj Singh: not cruel, not afraid. And here's the turn in his story. He was sent away to be forgotten, and Singapore is where he is remembered. Sikhs there keep his memorial, and people still come to pay their respects. The far-off place his captors chose became the place that holds his name. That's today's word.
screen: `A HOLY MAN WITH A DERA.` · `HE WOULD NOT SURRENDER.` · `SENT ACROSS THE SEA TO SINGAPORE.` · `AFRAID OF NO ONE.` · then, large: `REMEMBERED FAR AWAY.`

segments.voice: Two minutes for a far-off grave. Sit, and breathe slowly. Bring to mind someone who is buried, or whose ashes rest, far from where you are: a grandparent in another country, a friend in another city, an ancestor whose grave you've never seen. If no one comes, think of all those who died far from home. Picture the place, as best you can. Say their name in your mind. Let them be remembered for these two minutes, right here. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Bhai Maharaj Singh. A Sikh holy man who resisted British rule in Punjab, was exiled to Singapore and died there, where Sikhs keep his memorial. Today's word.

original.note: bhai, brother; a title of respect for a devout Sikh or a learned one.
